source.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

claims.summary: Parametric language-model knowledge is difficult to revise or inspect directly and does not straightforwardly provide provenance.
The paper proposes combining parametric generation with retrieval-based non-parametric memory so external knowledge can be inspected, expanded, or replaced.
The RAG architecture combines a query encoder and document index with a seq2seq generator, retrieves top-k documents by MIPS, and marginalizes generation over retrieved documents.

locator.label: Figure 1
locator.selection: Retriever, document index, generator, top-k documents, and marginalization flow

claims.summary: RAG-Sequence uses one latent retrieved document for the complete output sequence and marginalizes sequence probabilities across top-k documents.
RAG-Token allows a different latent retrieved document to support each generated token and marginalizes at each token step.
The retriever is initialized from DPR and uses separate dense document and query representations with MIPS over a document index.
The generator is BART-large, and the input sequence is concatenated with retrieved content before generation.
During task fine-tuning, the query encoder and generator are updated while the document encoder and document index remain fixed.
The experiments use one Wikipedia passage index across open-domain QA, abstractive QA, question generation, and fact verification tasks.
The paper extends retrieval-augmented models beyond extractive answering by conditioning a seq2seq generator on retrieved text.
On the Natural Questions test set, RAG-Sequence reports 44.5 Exact Match and DPR reports 41.5.

claims.summary: The index hot-swapping experiment demonstrates that changing the non-parametric Wikipedia index can update which time-specific facts the model answers without retraining the generator.
Because the external memory contains raw text, the authors describe it as human-readable and human-writable, enabling inspection and index updates.
The paper's broader-impact discussion warns that an external source such as Wikipedia can still contain factual errors and bias.

The authors conclude that users preferred RAG generations over parametric-only BART on the evaluated task, but frame future work around better interaction between parametric and non-parametric memory.
